title: Session 2: Confirming what came before

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: The Quran calls itself a confirmation of the Scripture before it and a guardian over it. The Bible gives its own tests for any later message. What are those tests, and how would you use them?

steps.question: The Quran says it confirms the Scripture before it and is "a watcher over it". What test does Isaiah give for any voice that claims to speak for God?

facts.text: Testimony is te'udah: "attestation". Isaiah sends every voice back "To the law and to the testimony".
Sale words 5:48 "preserving the same safe from corruption"; Pickthall, "a watcher over it". In both, the Quran guards the books before it.

steps.question: The Quran asks the children of Israel to believe what confirms "that which ye possess already". By what test did Moses tell Israel to judge a prophet, even one whose sign comes to pass?

facts.text: Sign is oth: "a signal", "evidence". In Deuteronomy 13 a sign that comes to pass is not enough: the test is whether the prophet says "Let us go after other gods".
The Quran (10:37) calls itself "a confirmation of that which was before it". Moses' test asks whether a new word leads to the same God: "Ye shall walk after the LORD your God".

steps.question: Moses promised a prophet "like unto thee". How does Israel know a word the LORD has not spoken, and to whom does Peter apply the promise?

facts.text: Many Muslim writers read Deuteronomy 18:18 as Muhammad, a prophet from the brethren of Israel. Peter applies the same words to Jesus: "A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me".
Moses' second test: if the thing "follow not, nor come to pass", the LORD has not spoken it.

steps.question: Paul writes about "another gospel". What does he say if even an angel from heaven preaches a different one?

facts.text: Accursed is anathema: "a (religious) ban". Paul puts himself under the test first: "though we, or an angel from heaven".
The Quran says it was brought by the angel Gabriel (2:97). Galatians 1:8 sets its test above any messenger, even an angel.

steps.question: How does John say to try the spirits, and what must a spirit confess?

facts.text: Try is dokimazo: "to test". John's test is a confession about Jesus Christ: "is come in the flesh".

steps.question: Jesus said he came not to destroy the law. What does he say will happen to the smallest letter of it?

facts.text: Fulfil is pleroo: "to make replete". A jot is yod, the smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

steps.question: Living it out: John says "try the spirits whether they are of God". How do these verses say we test what we hear?

facts.text: The Bereans "searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so"; Paul: "Prove all things; hold fast that which is good".

remember.text: "To the law and to the testimony"
A prophet with a sign who leads after other gods is not to be followed.
"though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel"
"every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God"
"one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law"
